title: HealthLog – Sleep & Activity
description: Sleep stages, sleep against activity on one scale, and which gap between them lines up.

list.name: tz
list.label: Timezone
list.description: Hidden. HealthLog's configured TZ (app_settings.local_tz), as in the upstream dashboards.
list.query: SELECT value FROM app_settings WHERE key = 'local_tz'
list.definition: SELECT value FROM app_settings WHERE key = 'local_tz'

list.name: shift
list.label: Activity counted
list.description: Which day's activity sits next to each night: the day you woke up, or N days later.
list.query: same day : 0, 1 day later : 1, 2 days later : 2, 3 days later : 3, 4 days later : 4, 5 days later : 5, 6 days later : 6, 7 days later : 7

options.content:
Each night is dated by the morning you woke up. Your watch estimates the stages from movement and heart rate, not a sleep lab, so the pattern over weeks says more than any single night.

Total sleep is time asleep, all stages together. Deep sleep is the slow-wave stage, when you are hardest to wake; most of it comes in the first half of the night. Core sleep is Apple's name for light sleep and usually fills most of the night. REM sleep is the stage with the most vivid dreaming; its stretches get longer towards morning, so a short night trims REM first. Awake counts brief wakings; everyone has some and most are never remembered.

Some measures only come from newer watches or once a feature is switched on. A panel that says not reported by your devices in this range means no data, never zero.

panels.title: Last night
panels.description: Total sleep, the most recent night recorded.

targets.rawSql: SELECT total_sleep_h AS "Total sleep" FROM sleep_nightly ORDER BY sleep_date DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Average night
panels.description: Mean total sleep over the nights in the selected range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT AVG(total_sleep_h) AS "Total sleep" FROM sleep_nightly WHERE $__timeFilter((sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))

panels.title: Nights recorded
panels.description: Nights with sleep data in the selected range. Nights without the watch are missing, not zero.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Nights" FROM sleep_nightly WHERE $__timeFilter((sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))

panels.title: REM share
panels.description: REM sleep as a share of total sleep over the range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 100 * SUM(rem_h) / NULLIF(SUM(total_sleep_h), 0) AS "REM" FROM sleep_nightly WHERE $__timeFilter((sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))

panels.title: Sleep stages per night
panels.description: Hours in each stage, stacked: the bar's height is time in bed asleep plus brief wakings.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz') AS time, deep_h AS "Deep", core_h AS "Core", rem_h AS "REM", awake_h AS "Awake" FROM sleep_nightly WHERE $__timeFilter((sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz')) ORDER BY sleep_date

defaults.noValue: Not reported by your devices in this range

options.content:
Reading the combined chart. Hours of sleep, minutes of exercise and steps don't share a scale, so each line shows where that day ranks among your own days on screen: 100 is your highest, 0 your lowest, and the grey line at 50 is a typical day. Ranking puts a long night and a big exercise day on the same footing, however different the units, and one extreme day can't flatten the rest. Each date shows that day's exercise and steps next to a night's sleep: by default the night you woke up from that morning. Activity counted at the top moves the sleep line forward, so with 1 day later Monday night's sleep (you wake on Tuesday) sits next to Wednesday's activity.

Peaks and dips that line up are worth a look, not proof: over a few weeks, lines can match by chance.

panels.title: Sleep and activity, ranked against your own days
panels.description: Each series as its percentile rank over the selected range: 100 = your highest day, 50 = typical, 0 = lowest.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT sleep_date + $shift AS day, total_sleep_h AS v FROM sleep_nightly WHERE $__timeFilter((sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))
), e AS (
  SELECT day, sum AS v FROM daily_metrics WHERE metric = 'apple_exercise_time' AND $__timeFilter((day::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))
), st AS (
  SELECT day, sum AS v FROM daily_metrics WHERE metric = 'step_count' AND $__timeFilter((day::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))
), days AS (SELECT day FROM s UNION SELECT day FROM e UNION SELECT day FROM st)
SELECT (day::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz') AS time,
  s.r AS "Sleep", e.r AS "Exercise", st.r AS "Steps"
FROM days
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT day, 100 * percent_rank() OVER (ORDER BY v) AS r FROM s) s USING (day)
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT day, 100 * percent_rank() OVER (ORDER BY v) AS r FROM e) e USING (day)
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT day, 100 * percent_rank() OVER (ORDER BY v) AS r FROM st) st USING (day)
ORDER BY day

defaults.noValue: Not reported by your devices in this range

panels.title: Exercise after longer and shorter nights
panels.description: Average exercise minutes after nights at or above your median sleep (longer) and below it (shorter), on the day set by Activity counted. A description, not a test.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT sleep_date AS day, total_sleep_h AS v FROM sleep_nightly WHERE $__timeFilter((sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))
), m AS (SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY v) AS mid FROM s),
a AS (
  SELECT s.day, s.v >= m.mid AS longer, d.metric, d.sum
  FROM s CROSS JOIN m JOIN daily_metrics d
    ON d.day = s.day + $shift AND d.metric IN ('apple_exercise_time', 'step_count')
)
SELECT CASE WHEN longer THEN 'After longer nights' ELSE 'After shorter nights' END
         || ' (' || COUNT(*) || ' days)' AS "Group",
       AVG(sum) AS "Value"
FROM a WHERE metric = 'apple_exercise_time' GROUP BY longer ORDER BY longer DESC

panels.title: Steps after longer and shorter nights
panels.description: Average steps after your longer and shorter nights (split at your median sleep), on the day set by Activity counted.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT sleep_date AS day, total_sleep_h AS v FROM sleep_nightly WHERE $__timeFilter((sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))
), m AS (SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY v) AS mid FROM s),
a AS (
  SELECT s.day, s.v >= m.mid AS longer, d.metric, d.sum
  FROM s CROSS JOIN m JOIN daily_metrics d
    ON d.day = s.day + $shift AND d.metric IN ('apple_exercise_time', 'step_count')
)
SELECT CASE WHEN longer THEN 'After longer nights' ELSE 'After shorter nights' END
         || ' (' || COUNT(*) || ' days)' AS "Group",
       AVG(sum) AS "Value"
FROM a WHERE metric = 'step_count' GROUP BY longer ORDER BY longer DESC

options.content:
Which gap lines up? Each bar measures how closely sleep and exercise or steps move together when they are a given number of days apart, from -1 (opposite) through 0 (unrelated) to +1 (in step). Days apart count from the morning you woke up. Right of centre, the sleep comes first: +1 pairs Monday night (waking Tuesday) with Wednesday. Left of centre, the activity comes first: -2 pairs Monday's activity with the night ending Wednesday morning. Hover a bar for how many pairs it rests on.

How tall a bar chance alone reaches depends on the pairs behind it: about 0.3 either way for 40 pairs, 0.2 for 100. Among 30 bars, one may pass that by luck too. A bar that stays tall as the range grows is the one to watch.

panels.title: How closely sleep and activity move together, by days apart
panels.description: Rank correlation (Spearman) between total sleep and each activity at every gap from 7 days before to 7 days after the night, over the selected range. + = sleep first, - = activity first.

targets.rawSql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT sleep_date AS day, total_sleep_h AS v FROM sleep_nightly WHERE $__timeFilter((sleep_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '$tz'))
), a AS (
  SELECT day, metric, sum AS v FROM daily_metrics WHERE metric IN ('apple_exercise_time', 'step_count')
), p AS (
  SELECT g.gap, a.metric, s.v AS sv, a.v AS av
  FROM s CROSS JOIN generate_series(-7, 7) AS g(gap) JOIN a ON a.day = s.day + g.gap
), r AS (
  SELECT gap, metric, rank() OVER (PARTITION BY gap, metric ORDER BY sv) AS rs,
         rank() OVER (PARTITION BY gap, metric ORDER BY av) AS ra
  FROM p
)
SELECT CASE WHEN gap > 0 THEN '+' ELSE '' END || gap AS "Days apart",
  corr(rs, ra) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'apple_exercise_time') AS "Exercise",
  corr(rs, ra) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'step_count') AS "Steps",
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'apple_exercise_time') AS "Pairs (exercise)",
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE metric = 'step_count') AS "Pairs (steps)"
FROM r GROUP BY gap ORDER BY gap
